goal: A CMS built on TapeDB, released as a product next to it, that runs entirely in the customer's own Cloudflare account (data in their Durable Objects and R2). Done means a team can model content in code, edit and publish it together in a Studio, and serve it to front ends, with no server to run.

approval.notes: Build it as its own product (tapedb/cms, private), with no mention of Sanity in the product. Deploys only as temporary test Workers from Brandon's terminal.

actors.name: Developer
actors.description: Defines content types in code and deploys the CMS to their account.

actors.name: Editor
actors.description: Writes drafts, publishes, manages releases and assets.

actors.name: Admin
actors.description: Everything an editor does, plus deleting documents and managing members.

actors.name: Front end
actors.description: A website or app reading published content anonymously.

requirements.title: Content types defined in code, validated on every write
requirements.rationale: The product's model: types in the repository, migrations generated, invalid content refused server-side.

requirements.title: Drafts and atomic publish and unpublish
requirements.rationale: Readers must never see half a document or a stale overwrite.

requirements.title: Members and roles decide who reads, writes, publishes and deletes
requirements.rationale: Contributors and editors are different jobs.

requirements.title: Datasets are isolated from each other
requirements.rationale: Staging and production content, or several sites, in one account.

requirements.title: Live co-editing: see changes and who is where, never lose an edit
requirements.rationale: Teams edit at the same time.

requirements.title: Front ends read published content, cached
requirements.rationale: Content is useless until a site can show it.

requirements.title: An editing Studio in the browser
Releases publish many documents as one
requirements.rationale: Launches change many pages at once.

requirements.title: Revision history and restore
requirements.rationale: Undo a bad publish; see who changed what.

requirements.title: Images and files with focal-point crops
Scheduled publishing
requirements.rationale: Publish at a set time without someone at the keyboard.

requirements.title: Search in the Studio and on sites
requirements.rationale: Useful past a few hundred documents.

requirements.title: Comments and editorial tasks
requirements.rationale: Deferred past v1; buildable later as TapeDB models with live queries.

requirements.title: Visual editing overlays on the live site
requirements.rationale: Deferred past v1; v1 previews drafts in the Studio.

requirements.title: Hosted add-ons (Canvas, media library service, variants, agents)
requirements.rationale: Hosted services outside the open-source product.

useCases.title: Define content types
preconditions: A CMS project with TapeDB installed
mainFlow: Developer declares types and fields in code
The CMS compiles them to document and draft models and write rules
TapeDB generates a migration
Developer commits and deploys
alternateFlows: A removed field requires an explicit data-loss flag
An invalid publish sent straight at the model is refused

acceptance.criterion: Types compile to models; incomplete or invalid publishes are refused, also when sent at the model directly; slugs unique; strong references block deletion

useCases.title: Publish a document
mainFlow: Editor opens the draft
Editor publishes at the draft's revision
The document and its revision are written and the draft removed in one transaction
Readers see the whole document as one change
alternateFlows: The document changed since the draft was read: publish refused, nothing changes
Two publishes from one revision: exactly one lands

acceptance.criterion: Readers see nothing before publish and the whole document after; stale and invalid publishes roll back whole
Typed reads and writes work in workerd and deployed

useCases.title: Work within a role
mainFlow: Contributor signs in
Contributor writes drafts
Editor publishes them; admin deletes when needed
alternateFlows: Contributor tries to publish, also straight at the model: refused

acceptance.criterion: Reader reads published only; contributor drafts but cannot publish; editor publishes but cannot delete; admin deletes
Revoking one session or all others takes effect

useCases.title: Keep datasets apart
mainFlow: Each dataset is its own workspace
A session is scoped to one dataset
alternateFlows: A claim for one dataset presented to another: 403

acceptance.criterion: A claim for one workspace is refused by another (403 wrong_workspace)

useCases.title: Edit together
preconditions: Two editors on the same document
mainFlow: Both see each other's presence on the document and field
Edits to different fields both land and appear live
A rich-text field is locked while one editor types
alternateFlows: The second editor is refused the lock until it is released or expires
Under load (20 editors autosaving), every save lands

acceptance.criterion: Different fields land; locked rich text loses no edit; lock races, expiry and maximum hold
Presence shows who is where
Live views keep order and follow relations
20 editors x 1 save/s x 30 s with 100 live queries, deployed: no failed save, p99 under 200 ms

useCases.title: Serve published content
mainFlow: The publish triggers a signed webhook to the delivery Worker
The Worker writes the document to R2 by id and slug
The front end reads it, cached
alternateFlows: Unsigned, wrongly signed or old deliveries are refused
A late delivery of an older revision changes nothing

acceptance.criterion: Publish reaches the delivery path, slug changes and unpublish follow, cache hits, bad deliveries refused (deployed)
Webhooks are signed, ordered and retried

useCases.title: Edit in the Studio
preconditions: The Studio served from the CMS Worker
mainFlow: Editor creates a document from a generated form
Edits rich text and an image
Reviews the changes and publishes
Views the history
alternateFlows: A reader sees no edit or review controls

acceptance.criterion: In a browser: create, edit, publish, upload an image, view history

useCases.title: Publish a release
preconditions: Versions of several documents grouped in a release
mainFlow: Editor publishes the release
Every version is applied, revisions written, the release closed, in one transaction
alternateFlows: One changed or invalid version refuses the whole release
Two concurrent publishes: one lands; the release cannot be reopened

acceptance.criterion: A release publishes across types at once; readers never see half; 1,000 versions publish whole

useCases.title: Restore an earlier revision
mainFlow: Editor views revisions with values and writer
Restores one into the draft
Publishes it as a new revision
alternateFlows: Revisions cannot be edited or written in another's name

acceptance.criterion: Each publish and unpublish leaves an immutable revision; restore and republish makes a new one

useCases.title: Use images
preconditions: An image field on a type
mainFlow: Editor uploads an image and sets the focal point
Front ends request resized, cropped WebP URLs

acceptance.criterion: File rules decide reads and writes
Resize, focal crop, WebP, cache hit, private refused (deployed)

useCases.title: Schedule a publish
mainFlow: Editor sets a time
A Workflow sleeps until then and publishes
alternateFlows: The schedule changed after it started: the old one does not fire

acceptance.criterion: A scheduled release publishes at its time; a changed schedule does not fire the old version

useCases.title: Search content
mainFlow: Editor types a query
Matching documents appear

acceptance.criterion: Text search finds a document after save

useCases.title: Import an export
preconditions: An export tarball from another CMS
mainFlow: Developer runs the importer
Documents, rich text, references and assets are mapped and loaded
A report lists rejected documents

acceptance.criterion: An export imports documents, rich text, references and assets and reports rejects

milestones.title: Studio
milestones.notes: Built in tapedb/cms with a Playwright walkthrough; the assessment's smoke test has not been recorded here.
